quote.text: Glass, china, and reputation are easily crack’d, and never well mended.
quote.author: Benjamin Franklin, Poor Richard’s Almanack

stories.kicker: The Arctic · signed in New York on Tuesday, published the same afternoon
stories.headline: Article XI binds a country that does not yet exist.
stories.dek: Two new American defence areas in Greenland, a veto over who may invest there — and a clause obliging Denmark and Nuuk to guarantee the choices of a state neither of them governs.

stories.kicker: The big picture · three markets, three different stories
stories.headline: The futures board says the oil crisis is over. The last physical print says it had not started.
stories.dek: On 15 September, dated Brent was assessed twenty-two dollars above the front contract. The paper price has fallen nine per cent since. The agency publishes the next physical print today.

stories.headline: The Fishbone Clinic
stories.dek: A photograph of a doorway went round Chinese social media this month. The sign translates itself, into one run-on English word. Behind it is the quiet re-cutting of a health system along the grain of what patients say, rather than what organs do.

stories.kicker: The bench · a tribunal decides what a resignation was
stories.headline: Nine thousand nine hundred dollars for the lost income, and nine thousand nine hundred for the harm.
stories.dek: The Employment Claims Tribunal ruled on Tuesday that a woman who resigned had in fact been dismissed — then doubled the award to price what the dismissal did to her.

stories.kicker: Buy it once · hard-shell luggage and carry-ons
stories.headline: The shell is not what breaks. Turn the case over and look at the wheels.
stories.dek: Screws or rivets is the whole test — and in this climate the part that dies first is a polyurethane tyre quietly hydrolysing in a cupboard between trips.

stories.kicker: Hangzhou · an accelerator announced at the Apsara conference
stories.headline: Two hundred and sixteen gigabytes, and nobody will say what kind of memory it is.
stories.dek: Alibaba’s chip arm put the Zhenwu V900 on a stand on Tuesday. The number on the placard is the one the American export rule was written to catch — if it is the memory the rule means.

stories.kicker: The kit · announced Tuesday, in shops on Thursday
stories.headline: Both earcups are separate wireless devices. The headband carries one power cable.
stories.dek: The Beats 360 is built so the parts that always die — pads, headband foam — are consumables you can buy. It is also the first flagship here with no wired path at all.

stories.kicker: The good life · two Panerai releases, published hours apart
stories.headline: A numbered watch that is not a limited edition, on a movement from 2016.
stories.dek: The caseback is engraved “Annual Production” over a blank plaque. On the same day the same house launched a 42mm three-hander at a twenty-fifth of the price.

stories.kicker: Screen & sound · sixty million, and two aggregators fourteen points apart
stories.headline: Not one critic filed a negative review. The Metascore is eighty-one.
stories.dek: Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil opened at $60.2m on ninety minutes of runtime. The gap between the two scoreboards is the more interesting number.

stories.kicker: The family desk · a paper published Monday, and the band it actually covers
stories.headline: Puberty timing at ten, read against executive function at sixty.
stories.dek: Ten thousand seven hundred and twenty-two children, plus a genetic causal test on six hundred thousand adults. The authors wrote their own headline: “limited clinical significance.”

stories.kicker: Down the rabbit hole · glassblowing and lampworking
stories.headline: The piece is finished when it is cool, not when you stop working it.
stories.dek: Two crafts share one word and almost no equipment. One needs a furnace that never switches off. The other is a torch bolted to a bench — and it is the one you can have.

stories.kicker: The long game · a pooled analysis of what your wrist already records
stories.headline: The metric that looks most like a consistency score predicted nothing at all.
stories.dek: Seven studies, 109,365 people. A flattened daily rhythm carried a hazard ratio of 1.46 for death from any cause. Day-to-day regularity carried none.

stories.kicker: The diary · two things on this page close before October does
stories.headline: A show that quietly added a week, and an exhibition that leaves for good on the eighteenth.
stories.dek: Every row was re-checked at a promoter, a venue or an official ticketing page. Where no price is published, this page says so rather than repeat an aggregator’s guess.
